scope: Proposition 4.5 (Projected-overlap paths) of the manuscript “All-temperature pressure for orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses” (preprints/All-temperature-pressure-for-orthogonally-invariant-Ising-spin-glasses-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 234 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ecaeb31108feca6f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 4.3, let p be the quantile of the total overlap. Then the entire group path is determined by p: pa(s) = ∫︂ p(s) 0 f′ a(Dp(r)) dr, da = ∫︂ 1 0 f′ a(Dp(r)) dr. (4.16) These formulas hold at t = 0, for repeated eigenvalues, and when Dp(p(s)) = 0. More generally, for a smooth scalar or matrix function f on [0, 1], the path lf (s) = ∫︂ p(s) 0 f′ (Dp(r)) dr, df = f(0) + ∫︂ 1 0 f′ (Dp(r)) dr (4.17) has symbol f(Dp(p(s))) and root p(0+)f′(Dp(p(0+))). Symbol and root uniquely determine a bounded-variation path.
